## India: Regulatory Updates & Board Operationalization

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has initiated the process to operationalize the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI), inviting applications for its Chairperson and members. This marks a crucial step towards establishing the enforcement body for the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA). Separately, IDfy won MeitY's NeGD DPDP Innovation Challenge, highlighting government efforts to foster privacy-enhancing technologies as India moves closer to full enforcement.

## India: Compliance Readiness & Challenges

As the DPDPA's compliance deadlines for 2026-27 draw closer, Indian enterprises, including MSMEs, are urged to prioritize data security at the source. Many companies are still assessing their readiness, with the specifics of the DPDP Rules 2025 providing further guidance on implementation requirements. The role of Consent Managers under the DPDPA is also gaining attention, particularly for Global Capability Centres (GCCs) operating in India, impacting their data processing frameworks.

## India: Legal Scrutiny & Interpretational Hurdles

The Supreme Court has issued notice regarding a constitutional challenge to the DPDPA, 2023, and the DPDP Rules, 2025, signaling potential legal battles ahead for the new privacy framework. Legal experts are also debating the absence of a statutory definition of "harm" within the DPDPA, raising concerns about interpretational uncertainty in future privacy adjudications. Furthermore, analyses highlight potential regulatory blind spots in India's data protection framework that may require future clarification or amendments.
